## KEYRENAME (rename FITS keywords including HIERARCH keywords)

**Frank Valdes** wrote on May 08, 2000

<pre style="background: transparent; box-shadow: none; border: none;">
# KEYRENAME - Rename FITS keywords.
# 
# A keyword translation file of the form
# 
#    xxxxxxxxx=yyyyyyy
# 
# is used to translate FITS keywords in the input text file to create an
# output text file.  All lines with no translation are left unchanged.  The
# file to be translated is often generated by the HFIX task from an image
# header.  Note that if the input and output filenames are the same then the
# modified version will replace the input version when the task completes.
# 
# The string
# to the left of the equal sign is matched exactly against the string to
# the left of the equal sign in the input file being edited.  Note that blanks
# are significant.  A common example is translating the ESO HIERARCH
# keywords using a translation file such as
# 
#   HIERARCH ESO GEN EXPO TYPE  = IMAGETYP
#   HIERARCH ESO INS OPTI-1 NAME= FILTER1
#    
# If a match is found the string to the right of the equal sign is
# substituted.  The substitution will be just the first word and it will be
# padded to the 8 character FITS keyword length.  In the above example
# the input and output lines will look like
# 
#   in:  HIERARCH ESO GEN EXPO TYPE  = &#x27;SCI&#x27;           / Type of exposure
#   in:  HIERARCH ESO INS OPTI-1 NAME= &#x27;ESO U&#x27;         / Filter name
# 
#   out: IMAGETYP= &#x27;SCI&#x27;           / Type of exposure
#   out: FILTER1 = &#x27;ESO U&#x27;         / Filter name
# 
# This task is commonly used with the task HFIX in a command such as:
# 
#     cl&gt; hfix eso.fits command=&quot;keyrename $fname $fname trans.dat&quot;
# 
# To define this task, copy it to your home directory.  Then in your login.cl
# or loginuser.cl files or interactive enter:
# 
#     task keyrename = home$keyrename.cl
# 


procedure keyrename (input, output, translation)

file	input		{prompt=&quot;Input filename&quot;}
file	output		{prompt=&quot;Output filename&quot;}
file	translation	{prompt=&quot;Translation filename&quot;}

struct	*fd1, *fd2

begin
	file	in, out, trans, tmp
	string	key1, value
	struct	line, key
	int	idx

	# Read query parameters.
	in = input
	out = output
	trans = translation

	# Set temporary file if the input and output filenames are the same.
	if (in == out)
	    tmp = mktemp (&quot;tmp$iraf&quot;)
	else
	    tmp = out

	# Scan each line in the input and translate.
	fd1 = in
	while (fscan (fd1, line) != EOF) {

	    # Find the equal sign and pass lines without one.
	    idx = stridx (&quot;=&quot;, line)
	    if (idx == 0) {
		printf (&quot;%s\n&quot;, line, &gt;&gt; tmp)
		next
	    }

	    # Extract the keyword part and the value part.
	    key = substr (line, 1, idx-1)
	    value = substr (line, idx, 80)

	    # Search for match in the translation file.
	    fd2 = trans
	    while (fscan (fd2, line) != EOF) {
		idx = stridx (&quot;=&quot;, line)
		if (idx == 0)
		    next

		key1 = substr (line, 1, idx-1)
		if (key1 == key) {
		    key1 = substr (line, idx+1, 80)

		    # Strip whitespace and format to 8 characters.
		    printf (&quot;%s\n&quot;, key1) | scan (key1)
		    printf (&quot;%-8.8s\n&quot;, key1) | scan (key)

		    break
		}
	    }
	    fd2 = &quot;&quot;

	    # Output line with translation if one was found.
	    printf (&quot;%s%s\n&quot;, key, value, &gt;&gt; tmp)
	}
	fd1 = &quot;&quot;

	# Replace input with output if the names are the same.
	if (in == out) {
	    delete (in, verify-)
	    rename (tmp, out, field=&quot;all&quot;)
	}
end
</pre>
